**Title (English, from literature):** The training rule on lying

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 1 (*Musāvāda*), translated by Bhikkhu Brahmali as "The training rule on lying", is the opening rule of the Pācittiya section of the Theravāda *Vinaya Piṭaka*. The rule establishes that a monastic who intentionally speaks an untruth commits an offense requiring formal confession [Collins 1993; Hüsken 1997]. It introduces the first ten pācittiyas, which comprise the *Musāvādavagga* ("chapter on lying") [Collins 1993]. In doctrinal analyses of moral transgression, scholars note that while Pācittiya 1 governs deliberate lying in general (*sampajānamusā bhāsitum*), it is distinguished from Pārājika 4, where a specific, grave category of falsehood—falsely claiming higher superhuman attainments (*uttarimanussadhamma*)—constitutes an offense entailing irreversible expulsion from the Saṅgha [Collins 1993; Hüsken 1997].
